div.div:
A two-way door.
Traffic can come in and go out through it. AWS runs it for you, it never fills up, and it costs nothing by itself.

text.tspan: Traffic can come in and go out through it. AWS runs it for you,
it never fills up, and it costs nothing by itself.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 332px; height: 1px; padding-top: 165px; margin-left: 643px;

div.div:
Only the public subnet uses it.
Its route table says “anything for the internet, go via the internet gateway”. That one line is what makes a subnet public.

Its route table says “anything for the internet, go via the
internet gateway”. That one line is what makes a subnet

div.div:
The private subnet has no such line.
Nobody on the internet can reach it directly, even if they know its address. Customers only ever talk to the load balancer.
